summary: Genuine counter-evidence attempts made for all five target claims (A-E) using GitHub issue/PR search (api.github.com, unauthenticated), direct primary-source-code fetch, and forum/HN search where reachable. Claim A (smooth build) weakened: three independent GitHub artifacts on SIGRobotics-UIUC/LeKiwi (issue #17 camera-mount fit mismatch; PR #9 maintainer-merged drive-motor-mount rigidity redesign; PR #26 unmerged servo-mount stability redesign) show the print files have had real, externally-discovered design shortcomings, though none rise to documented warping/breakage/heat-set-insert failure and the sole build-log account (Foxglove) still reports a smooth build (confidence 0.35). Claim D (motor-ID pitfall) resolved and strengthened, not weakened: direct inspection of the official huggingface/lerobot source (lekiwi.py) confirms the 7/8/9-to-wheel-position mapping is hardcoded software, universal rather than Seeed-specific, corroborated by independent issue #1243 documenting real wheel-ID setup friction (confidence 0.85, reported per plan guidance as a successful resolved check). Claims B (no heat-set inserts), C (time estimates), and E (real-world spend) held at low confidence: targeted GitHub searches turned up no on-topic counter-evidence, and the broader Reddit/YouTube/forum/general-web search angles specified in the plan could not be executed due to tooling gaps -- WebSearch budget was already exhausted session-wide before this step began, Reddit returned HTTP 403 to direct fetch, Google/Bing/DuckDuckGo results pages did not render usable content or hit a CAPTCHA via WebFetch, YouTube/Hackaday.io search pages are JS-rendered and returned no content via WebFetch, and the agent-browser skill's dependency (belt CLI) is not installed/authenticated in this environment. Seeed Studio's own community forum returned zero LeKiwi results (a genuine negative, not a tooling failure). These are named, explicit gaps per the plan's own instructions, not conflated with resolved absence of the underlying issues.
